title: refactor(ci): consolidate lint/test/release workflows, bump actions and Node 20
author: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Consolidate the repository's CI workflows to reduce duplication and speed up developer feedback loops. This PR merges the separate lint, test, and release GH Actions workflows into a small set of reusable workflows and shared composite actions. It also standardizes on Node 20 runners, bumps GitHub Actions used across workflows to the latest supported versions, and improves caching for monorepo packages to reduce CI time.

Motivation: Over time multiple workflow files diverged with duplicate steps (install, cache, setup-node) and inconsistent job matrices. This surfaced in flaky CI times and maintenance overhead. Consolidation reduces surface area for infra drift and makes future changes (e.g. new Node versions, caching strategies) one place to update.

Changes included (high level):
- New workflows: .github/workflows/ci.yml (lint + test matrix), .github/workflows/release.yml (release automation and tagging), .github/workflows/build-cache.yml (build & cache priming)
- Introduced composite actions under .github/actions/shared-setup to centralize node/npm/yarn setup, caching and matrix expansion
- Bumped actions/setup-node to v4, actions/checkout to v4, and setup-java where used; migrated deprecated uses
- Standardized Node runtime to 20.x with a compatibility matrix (16 -> 18 -> 20 jobs kept for targeted packages)
- Improved cache keys to include lockfile + package.json hash to avoid stale installs
- Fixed CI flakes by adding retry wrapper around a known-racy e2e step and increased test timeout for slow Windows runners
- Reduced duplicated job definitions across repositories in the monorepo (moved common steps into composite actions)

Testing & validation:
- Local workflow.run tests using act for sanity checks (where supported)
- Multiple CI runs on this PR validated passes across linux/mac/windows matrices
- Back-compat verified for release automation: tagging and changelog generation flows ran successfully in a dry-run environment

Checklist:
- [x] Consolidate lint + test jobs into single CI workflow with matrices
- [x] Move reusable steps into composite actions under .github/actions/shared-setup
- [x] Bump relevant actions and add notes to docs/ci.md
- [x] Keep compatibility jobs for Node 16/18 for legacy packages where needed
- [x] Validate caching strategy and measure wall-clock savings (~22% median CI time reduction in preliminary runs)
- [x] Run release dry-run and confirm changelog and tag automation

Links: Linear: https://linear.app/issue/ENG-4321, SUP ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-1189

Notes for reviewers: The functional changes are primarily in workflow orchestration; runtime/package changes are minimal. I extracted the smallest possible patches to composite actions to make subsequent per-repo stabilization easier. If you want to review the net effects on a per-package basis I can provide a follow-up PR that reintroduces a legacy workflow for a single package and runs a longer compatibility matrix (kept out of this change to reduce PR scope).
commits: feat(ci): add ci.yml consolidating lint and test matrices
chore(actions): add shared composite action for node/install/cache
fix(ci): retry flaky e2e step and increase timeout for windows runner
docs: update docs/ci.md with workflow and caching guidance
file_snippets:
--- .github/workflows/ci.yml (excerpt) ---
jobs:
  test:
    strategy:
      matrix:
        node: [16, 18, 20]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: ./.github/actions/shared-setup
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}

--- .github/actions/shared-setup/action.yml (excerpt) ---
runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Setup node
      uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: ${{ inputs.node-version }}
    - name: Restore cache
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        key: ${{ inputs.cache-key }}
review_comments: Miguel Ramirez: Looks good overall. Can you add a short note explaining when we keep Node 16/18 jobs? I want to avoid surprise CI debt.

Priya Patel: CI times look good, but one of the Windows jobs still flakes intermittently. Recommend we skip that specific slow package on windows for now.
Ava Chen: Skipped the failing package on windows and added TODO with a link to ENG-4510 for remediation.
Liam O'Connor: Approved after resolving doc comment and ensuring release dry-run succeeded.

release_notes: Refactor CI workflows: consolidated lint/test/release workflows into smaller reusable workflows
Bumped GitHub Actions (setup-node v4, checkout v4) and standardized on Node 20 with compatibility matrix
Improved caching and reduced median CI time by ~22% (preliminary)
Non-breaking: kept Node 16/18 compatibility jobs for selected legacy packages
summary: Consolidates and modernizes CI workflows, bumps actions, standardizes Node 20, and improves caching to reduce CI maintenance and runtime.
